paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about Ruth 1. Nobody in this chapter has it figured out. Naomi loses her husband and both her sons, and she says, "I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty." (Ruth 1:21) She doesn't dress it up, and she doesn't pretend. I think that's honest, and I think the Bible lets her be honest.

Then comes Ruth. Naomi gives her every good reason to turn around, and Ruth says, "your people will be my people, and your God will be my God." (Ruth 1:16) She doesn't have a plan, and she doesn't have a guarantee. She just stays, and she stays with the LORD's people. That's what loyal love looks like when nothing is going your way, friend. It shows up and keeps showing up.

And look at the last line. Two widows walk into Bethlehem "at the beginning of the barley harvest." (Ruth 1:22) Naomi thinks she's empty, but she walked back home to a town where the LORD had provided food, and she didn't walk alone. So when your own season feels empty, baker, don't quit the road. Stay close to the people of God and keep walking toward Him, because this story is NOT done.
